findings.statement: CA9 is tumor-cell intrinsic: the RCC cluster holds almost all tumor transcripts of the gene [gene=CA9; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=RCC; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.976], and in donor-paired pseudobulk tumor cells are far above proximal tubule [gene=CA9; type=sc_tumor_vs_pt; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; log2fc=7.739]. It ranks first in the convergence ranking and is purity-robust and replicated in TCGA, but ccRCC DepMap effect is near zero and the gene has no prognostic signal, so it is a biomarker and antibody/imaging target rather than a proven dependency.

The AlphaFold model of CA9 is moderately confident overall [gene=CA9; type=alphafold_model; source=DATASET:ALPHAFOLD-DB; mean_plddt=76.56]; its top cavity has a small volume [gene=CA9; type=structural_context; source=DATASET:ALPHAFOLD-DB; volume_a3=126.8] and detected cavities recover about half of experimental ligand-contact residues (recall in ligand_site_validation). This is a descriptive monomer heuristic and says nothing about degrons, ligase compatibility or degradation.

CD70 is highest per cell in RCC cells (largest cpm_share) but Tregs, CD8 T and B cells also express it, and CD8 T cells carry a large share of transcripts only because of their number, so the bulk signal is mixed. It is still tumor-up, replicated in TCGA and purity-robust, and already has clinical anti-CD70 agents; no selective ccRCC dependency is shown.

KDR is an endothelial microenvironment target, not a tumor-cell target: endothelial cells hold nearly all its tumor transcripts [gene=KDR; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=Endothelial; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.951], while RCC cells are not among the expressing groups in the summary.

EPAS1 (HIF-2a) is not mainly a tumor-cell transcript in this dataset: endothelial cells express it in most cells [gene=EPAS1; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=Endothelial; tissue=tumor; pct_expressing=81.3] whereas RCC cells express it in few cells [gene=EPAS1; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=RCC; tissue=tumor; pct_expressing=4.9]. Bulk EPAS1 signal therefore reflects endothelium and fibroblasts at least as much as tumor cells; this may partly be low dropout-prone detection of a transcription factor.

MET transcripts in tumor are mostly in RCC cells [gene=MET; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=RCC; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.935], with a minor endothelial contribution, so it is a tumor-cell-attributed kinase target.

EGFR transcripts are mostly in RCC cells [gene=EGFR; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=RCC; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.948], but only a minority of RCC cells express it, so expression is heterogeneous across tumor cells.

CD74 is an immune (antigen-presenting) transcript, not tumor-intrinsic: macrophages hold the largest share [gene=CD74; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=Macrophage; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.436], with cDC highest per cell and CD8 T cells contributing a large share by cell number.

CXCR4 is expressed by lymphocytes, not tumor cells; CD8 T cells hold the largest transcript share [gene=CXCR4; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=CD8_T; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.563], and CD4 T, B, Treg and pDC cells also express it, so it is an immune-microenvironment target.

COL23A1 is the top tumor-track candidate: RCC cells hold most of its transcripts [gene=COL23A1; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=RCC; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.881], it is replicated in TCGA and remains up in a pure tumour [gene=COL23A1; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=tumor; rna_lfc_at_purity1=4.88]. It has few ccRCC papers, no clinical drug, is annotated as cell-membrane (UniProt only; SURFY and CSPA do not support it) and has no vital-organ protein enrichment, but it has no selective DepMap dependency, no adverse prognosis, and only a minority of RCC cells express it.

The COL23A1 AlphaFold model is low confidence overall [gene=COL23A1; type=alphafold_model; source=DATASET:ALPHAFOLD-DB; mean_plddt=58.91] and its only detected cavity is tiny and shallow with a low structural-context score, so small-molecule tractability is poor; an antibody against the extracellular domain is the more plausible modality, and this heuristic does not exclude other approaches.

RAB42 is a second tumor-track hypothesis: RCC cells hold most of its transcripts, it is replicated in TCGA and purity-robust, has very few ccRCC papers and no clinical drug, but is internal (not antibody-accessible), has no selective dependency or prognostic signal, and its model is well folded [gene=RAB42; type=alphafold_model; source=DATASET:ALPHAFOLD-DB; mean_plddt=85.31] with only small cavities.

OLFML2A is a stroma-track candidate carried by fibroblasts, secreted, with very few ccRCC papers and no clinical drug; it is replicated in TCGA and purity-robust with no adverse survival, but expression in colon and other organs and the lack of a dependency or functional evidence limit it to a hypothesis on a secreted stromal marker.

COX4I2 is a stroma-track hypothesis made mostly by fibroblasts; it is replicated in TCGA and purity-robust with no adverse survival, but it is an internal mitochondrial protein (not antibody-accessible) with high lung expression, so it is unlikely to be a clean therapeutic target.

GAL3ST4 is a macrophage-derived internal enzyme with almost no ccRCC literature and an adverse-prognosis direction that remains after purity adjustment, but it is not surface-accessible and has no dependency or functional data, so it is only a biomarker-type hypothesis.

caveats: Single-cell attribution comes from 12 donors; endothelial, fibroblast and PT groups have few cells or donors, so shares are unstable. Transcript share depends on how many cells of each type were captured.
EPAS1 and other transcription factors are poorly detected in scRNA-seq, which may understate tumor-cell expression.
Discovery candidates are data-ranked hypotheses with no dependency or functional evidence; literature is counted by gene symbol.
Structural-context scores describe predicted monomer cavities and do not identify degrons, ligase compatibility or predict degradation.

The CD70 single-cell record had no evidence id, so its cell attribution is stated in words only; CD74 and CXCR4 purity checks and ccRCC-specific DepMap data for the microenvironment genes were not run; the EPAS1 tumor-versus-PT test was not run.
The PubMed connector requires authorization and was not used.
